assays.assay_description: Rectangular chamber (35 × 20 × 30 cm) with aluminum walls, Plexiglas front/ceiling and stainless-steel grid floor. Day 1: 3-min habituation; Day 2: conditioning (3 × 0.7 mA, 3 s footshocks); Day 3: 3-min retrieval/reactivation session; Aya 60 mg/kg o.g. or water given 20 min before or 3 h after retrieval; Day 4: 3-min Test. Freezing (%) scored manually by a blinded observer during retrieval and Test.

application_type.evidence: all animals received Aya or Veh via oral gavage (o.g.)

setup_habituation.evidence: animals were individually placed in the chamber for a 3 min habituation session and were allowed to explore the context

time_to_assay.evidence: Twenty min before or 3 h after retrieval each cohort of animals received Aya or Veh... The next day, rats underwent a 3 min exposure to the conditioned context (Test). Timepoints: retrieval 20 min post-drug (-20 min group); Test ~24 h 20 min post-drug (-20 min group) or ~21 h post-drug (3 h group).

sample_size.evidence: Forty-one rats were assigned to one of the four conditioned groups... Number of animals per group:-20 min: Veh = 10; Aya = 11; 3 h: Veh = 10; Aya = 10

outcomes.summary: Ayahuasca (60 mg/kg, o.g.) given 20 min before or 3 h after fear memory retrieval significantly reduced freezing during the 3-min Test 24 h later relative to vehicle, indicating impaired fear memory reconsolidation; the effect did not depend on the timing of administration. Retrieval freezing did not differ between groups in the plasticity and neurogenesis cohorts.
outcomes.statistics: Two-way RM ANOVA: treatment F(1,37)=25.5, p=0.00001, η2=0.41; repetition F(1,37)=22.4, p=0.00003, η2=0.37; time of treatment F(1,37)=0.56, p=0.46; treatment × repetition × time F(1,37)=0.00013, p=0.99; repetition × treatment F(1,37)=29.3, p=0.000001, η2=0.44; repetition × time of treatment F(1,37)=8.2, p=0.007, η2=0.18; Tukey post hoc: Aya reduced freezing at both timings. Retrieval (Exp 2): -20 min t14=0.004, p=0.97; 3 h t15=1.345, p=0.199. Retrieval (Exp 3): -20 min t7=0.95, p=0.37; 3 h t9=0.238, p=0.81.
outcomes.evidence: Tukey's post hoc analysis of treatment and repetition interaction showed that Aya treatment significantly reduced freezing behavior in both moments (Fig. 1b). Together, the results suggest that Aya treatment impaired fear memory reconsolidation, regardless of the moment of administration.

judge_notes: All three candidates identified a single behavioural assay (contextual fear conditioning); Golgi-Cox spine analysis and DCX immunohistochemistry are histological endpoints and were excluded per rubric.

Retrieval-session freezing recorded in Experiments 2 and 3 cohorts merged into the same fear-conditioning assay; n reported from the Experiment 1 cohort (41 rats), which is the only cohort with the Test session.
D4 baseline scored 1 (modal, 2/3): retrieval freezing was recorded before drug for the 3 h group; confidence medium since the -20 min group received drug before retrieval.
D5 follow-up scored 0 (modal, 2/3): Test was ~21 h after dosing for the 3 h group; only the -20 min group marginally exceeds 24 h.
